question: Why do I wet my hands?
expected: So the rice doesn't stick to your fingers, and you can spread it gently without squashing the grains (the chef says so).

question: Which side of the nori goes down?
expected: Shiny side down; the rough side holds the rice.

question: Which way round does the nori sheet go?
expected: Long edge towards you, flat on the bamboo mat.

question: How thick should the rice be?
expected: A thin, even layer: you should still see the dark nori through the rice in places.

question: Why do I leave bare nori at the far edge?
expected: About two centimetres of bare nori along the far edge seals the roll.

question: What do beginners usually get wrong?
expected: They use far too much rice, and then the roll won't close.

question: How much filling should I use?
expected: Just one thin line of cucumber across the third of the sheet closest to you.

question: What happens if I pile up the filling?
expected: It squeezes out when you roll.

question: How do I roll it?
expected: Lift the near edge of the mat, tuck the nori over the filling, roll forward and press gently along the whole length so it holds its shape.

question: How many pieces do I cut it into?
expected: Six even pieces: wet the knife, cut the roll in half, then cut each half into three.
